newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Veteran Singapore opposition politician sued.
newsitem.headline: Veteran Singapore opposition politician sued.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and 10 other ruling People's Action Party (PAP) members are suing veteran Workers' Party leader Joshua Jeyaretnam for allegedly defaming them, the Straits Times newspaper said.

Since Singapore's general election on January 2, in which the ruling PAP won 81 of 83 parliamentary seats, leading PAP politicians have issued a total of nine writs against Workers' Party activist Tang Liang Hong.
This is the first action against Jeyaretnam.
The 11 plaintiffs claim that Jeyaretnam used words at a Workers' Party rally on January 1 to allege they were guilty of criminal defamation and conspiracy and lacked honesty and integrity.
The Straits Times reported that Jeyaretnam had offered to apologise to the 11 plaintiffs but denied that he had used defamatory words.
Lawyers for the plaintiffs were unavailable for comment. Jeyaretnam was also unavailable.
Jeyaretnam was beaten in the elections but will take a seat in parliament anyway under a constitutional provision for a seat for best-loser if only two opposition members are elected to parliament.

Jeyaretnam made history in 1981 when he became the first opposition Member of Parliament when he won a by-election, the first opposition seat since independence in 1965. He later retained the Anson seat in the 1984 general election.
Troubles started for him shortly after he was re-elected.

In November 1986, the high court sentenced Jeyaretnam and Wong Hong Tay, then chairman of the Workers' Party to one month's imprisonment and a fine of S$5,000 (US$3,550) each on charges of making false statements about the party's accounts.
The conviction both disqualified Jeyaretnam from serving in Parliament and barred him from recontesting for five years.
But, appealing against the conviction to the Privy Council in London, Jeyaretnam on November 21, 1988, won a widely publicised condemnation of what had happened.
When the two petitioned President Wee Kim Wee for a pardon on the council's advice, the request was turned down. ($1 = S$1.41)
